title: Redwood discovery - model selection - Pinecrest AI
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
summary: Initial discovery focused on model selection and deployment mode. Pinecrest needs a multilingual model with at least 32k context for long-document summarization and tool-calling to hit internal systems. Security team flagged SOC2/SAML and KMS as requirements; product team cares about latency and cost. Discussed tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC) options and recommended benchmark pilot on both hosted and dedicated with 32k and 8k variants.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick introductions? We'll run 45 minutes, goal is model selection and deployment path.
[00:28] Alex (Pinecrest): Hi, Alex here, CTO. We're building long-form summarization and a customer insights product, need multilingual support.
[01:05] Maya (Pinecrest): Maya, ML eng. Running an internal ETL, we push ~200 documents per user, some reach 60k tokens; typical session we'll need 20-40k context sometimes.
[02:10] Sam (Pinecrest): Sam, product. Main success metric: summary accuracy and 95th pct latency under 2.5s for snippet-level queries, and acceptable batch latencies for full-doc jobs.
[05:00] Aisha (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. A couple quick clarifying Qs - by 60k tokens do you mean you'd like the model to see the full history in one shot, or can we pre-chunk / use KV cache?
[08:00] Maya: Prefer single-pass when feasible, because we want coherence across document sections. We can chunk but would prefer native long context if it's accurate.
[12:00] Priya (Pinecrest Security): From security side, must be SOC two compliant, SSO via SAML/Okta, and keys stored in our KMS/HSM. We also need audit logs and per-route RBAC.
[16:30] Luca (Redwood): That's all supported across Redwood Dedicated and Private. Hosted has SOC2 and SAML integrations, but for customer-managed KMS and on-prem HSM we usually recommend our Private offering. For Dedicated, we provide a VPC peering option and key management integrations.
[21:00] Jordan: Back to models - you're asking about open models. We typically evaluate Llaama-3 variants, Mistral-large, Falcon-180B, and some distilled Vicuna variants. For 32k+ contexts we saw Llama-3 70B and some Mistral forks do well, but there's tradeoffs in latency and cost.
[25:00] Maya: Any experience with 65k or 128k contexts? We might pilot 65k for a small subset.
[30:00] Aisha: There are emerging 64k-context forks; however, actual performance depends on kernel support and quantization. For 64k you often need dedicated GPUs with adequate memory (A100 80GB or H100) and you pay in throughput. Our recommendation is: pilot with a 32k profile first, measure degradation on larger contexts with streaming + KV caching.
[34:00] Alex: Tool-calling - we need function calling to hit internal search and a retrieval system. Does Redwood support structured tool calls across hosted and private? Any known model limits?
[38:00] Luca: Yes, function/tool calling is supported. It's model-dependent for native structured output; Redwood adds a shim that can help normalize outputs. For hosted, we have pre-wired connectors and schema validation; for Private you can run the same shim locally. Just note that some smaller open models hallucinate JSON schemas more often.
[41:30] Priya: On data residency - some customers need EU-only. Do you have regional hosting?
[44:45] Jordan: Yes, we have regional endpoints in EU and NA, and Private lets you keep everything in your VPC. Recap: we recommend a two-track pilot: hosted quick PoC with 8k and 32k variants to measure quality and latency, and a Dedicated pilot with a 32k profile on a few reserved nodes to test throughput and KV caching. We'll share a model-performance spreadsheet and pricing for both options.

Notes: transcription has a few mis-heard product names (e.g., LlaaMa vs Llama), some acronyms like SOC two transcribed as SOC two. There was occasional crosstalk; speaker labels may be approximate.
